title: Personal Credit Cards: Balance Owed as Counted from the Card Ledger
content:
The fixed sum of the automatic payment that stays on a Personal Credit Cards account being closed starts from the card's balance owed, counted from the entries on the card's ledger.

## What the figure is meant to be

The closing instruction is meant to gather no more than the cardholder still owes after the closing has been put in order. An annual fee that the charter does not let stand on a card closed inside that fee's refund window is not owed.

## How the figure is counted

The balance owed is read from the card's ledger as it stands when the matter is handled: the total of every entry that adds to the debt, less the total of every entry that reduces it.

| Adds to the debt | Reduces the debt |
|---|---|
| purchases | payments |
| cash advances | merchant credits |
| balance transfers | fee reversals |
| fees | interest reversals |
| interest charges | dispute credits |
| returned payments | rewards statement credits |
| rebilled dispute credits | |

Only entries present on the ledger enter the count. A fee billed to the card leaves the figure through its fee reversal entry and in no other way.

## Worked example (hypothetical entries)

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Purchases | 1850.00 |
| Cash advances | 200.00 |
| Fees | 105.00 |
| Interest charges | 38.40 |
| Total adding to the debt | 2193.40 |
| Payments | 600.00 |
| Merchant credits | 45.00 |
| Fee reversals | 95.00 |
| Total reducing the debt | 740.00 |
| Balance owed | 1453.40 |
